name: Feed grade dry whey; from cheese production; at dairy plant; dry weight basis
description: This system process is a cradle-to-gate dataset of production of one kg dry whey from cheese production in the United States.

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: Represents production at the national level.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: The unit process was converted to system process. The unit process is built from survey data which included raw milk, skim milk, cream, electricity, energy, water, packaging, clean-in-place chemicals, and water treatment. Full inventory is given in Kim et al. (2013).
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Life cycle inventory was originally assembled using the SimaPro software platform (Version 8.0.4.26) and was modified for submission using the OpenLCA platform (Version 1.3.0).
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Cheese-Whey allocation. See Kim et al. (2013)
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: This system process contains only substances. The original unit process included raw milk, skim milk, cream, electricity, energy, water, packaging, clean-in-place chemicals, and water treatment. See also, Nutter and Kim (2012).
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: This system process was built was adopted from a different project which was published in Nutter, D. and D.S. Kim 2011.

sources.name: Development of Life Cycle Inventory data for U.S. Swine Production Scenarios

reviews.details: University of Arkansas swine dataset mapped to USLCI technosphere flows and FEDEFL elementary flows for publication on the Federal LCA Commons. Review covers mapping crosswalks, cutoff flows, and export structure.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication: These data may be used in Situation C2, “Accounting without interactions.”  This is applicable to accounting studies that according to their goal definition do not include any interaction with other systems.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: University of Arkansas and Michigan Technological University Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Production of Fluid Milk in the US.
